title.value: Technology-enhanced trauma training in low-resource settings: A scoping review and feasibility analysis of educational technologies
title.justification: The title accurately reflects the main focus of the paper, which is the evaluation of educational technologies for trauma training in low-resource settings.
title.quote: Technology-enhanced trauma training in low-resource settings: A scoping review and feasibility analysis of educational technologies

extractions.description: The paper reviews and evaluates the feasibility of educational technologies used for trauma training in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). It identifies the strengths and limitations of various technologies such as high-fidelity mannequins and virtual simulation, with an emphasis on their applicability for low-resource settings. The study highlights the need for effective, feasible educational tools for trauma training in these regions.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central theme of the paper focuses on improving trauma training in low-resource settings, which connects to sustainable development goals related to health and education.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Given the urgent need for pediatric trauma training, educators must use technologies that optimize learning outcomes and remain feasible for low-resource settings.

primary_category.justification: The study directly addresses capacity-building in low- and middle-income countries by evaluating educational technologies that can improve trauma training in these regions, a critical aspect of supporting the Global South.
primary_category.quote: We identified that the majority of trauma courses in the literature use technologies which are less suitable for LMICs.

secondary_categories.justification: While the primary focus is on educational technologies for trauma training, the broader context of improving healthcare systems and resilience in LMICs can be linked to climate adaptation concerns, as stronger healthcare systems are crucial for adapting to climate impacts.
secondary_categories.quote: Educational technologies present a unique opportunity to enhance the quality of trauma training.

primary_sub_category.justification: By evaluating and recommending feasible educational technologies for trauma training in LMICs, the paper provides valuable knowledge and policy guidance for healthcare systems in these regions.
primary_sub_category.quote: Therefore, this study reviews current technologies used in trauma courses and evaluates their feasibility for LMICs.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper indirectly contributes to relief efforts by proposing better education and training methods that are critical during trauma-related emergencies, hence supporting efficient relief operations.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Despite their effectiveness, high-fidelity mannequins ranked poorly in production, maintenance, cost, and reusability categories, therefore being poorly suited for LMICs.

applications.value: Virtual simulation and digital courses for trauma training in LMICs
applications.justification: The study highlights virtual simulation and digital courses as feasible and effective solutions for trauma training in low-resource settings.
applications.quote: Virtual simulation and digital courses had the best feasibility scores, but still represented a minority of articles in our review.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper's focus fits within existing Sustainable Development categories related to support for the Global South and educational improvements therein.
new_primary_category.quote: To our knowledge, this is the first study to perform a feasibility analysis of trauma training technologies in the LMIC context.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The identified sub-categories of Policy Advice and Knowledge Sharing, and Relief Efforts sufficiently describe the paper's focus areas without needing a new sub-category.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: educators must use technologies that optimize learning outcomes and remain feasible for low-resource settings.
